components.name: Horizon Timer
components.description: The only stable, human-scale control in the field.
components.css: .ds-timer { background: transparent; border: 0; color: #f4e3c6; font-family: Bodoni Moda, Baskerville, Georgia, serif; font-optical-sizing: auto; font-size: clamp(3rem, 6.2vw, 6rem); font-variant-numeric: lining-nums tabular-nums; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: -0.065em; line-height: .86; padding: 2rem; text-align: center; } .ds-timer span { color: #c8b69a; display: block; font-family: Familjen Grotesk, Helvetica Neue, Arial, sans-serif; font-size: .66rem; font-weight: 500; letter-spacing: .1em; margin-top: .7rem; } .ds-timer:hover, .ds-timer:focus-visible { color: #fff7e8; outline: 1px solid #f4a83c; outline-offset: .35rem; }

components.name: Start-Time Field
components.description: A native date-time field with only one warm focus rule.
components.css: .ds-time { background: transparent; border: 0; border-bottom: 1px solid rgba(244,227,198,.35); border-radius: 0; color: #f4e3c6; min-height: 3rem; padding: .4rem 0; } .ds-time:hover, .ds-time:focus-visible { border-bottom-color: #f4a83c; outline: 0; }

narrative.overview: Timer Horizon is an after-hours scientific instrument: a full-screen typographic current collapsing toward a luminous central event horizon. The central duration is the only calm, human-scale object inside an otherwise black core. Everything else—abstract glyphs, living figures, and light—arrives from beyond the field and vanishes at the rim.
keyCharacteristics: A composed duration inside a breathing accretion ring.
A soot-dark field, mineral text, and hot stellar light.
A broad, readable letter-and-number infall, orbiting fact bodies, a precessing rim, a cursor wake, and a resilient HTML content layer.
No cards, graph furniture, terminal tropes, or chrome-heavy controls.

rules.name: The One-Star Rule
rules.body: The event horizon is the only major saturated form. Facts can borrow its pale heat; nothing else competes with it. Its breathing rim and precessing seam keep that focal point alive.

rules.name: The Human-Clock Rule
rules.body: The duration always uses words such as 5 minutes, 12 seconds, never a digit-only stopwatch.

dos: Do make readable glyph streams occupy the full field, then bend, shear, accelerate, and disappear at the event horizon.
Do keep facts readable as stable numerical bodies with smaller mineral-toned explainers directly beneath them, visibly separate from the abstract glyph field.
Do preserve the central duration and accessible content when effects are unavailable.
donts: Don't render fake code, terminal windows, charts, HUD brackets, or literal black-hole imagery.
Don't use rainbow color, green-on-black hacker styling, or multiple glowing focal points.
Don't distort the central timer or allow glyphs or facts inside the black core.
